title: Climbing the Fusion Tree: Center Ordering and Decoding Hierarchy in Non-Abelian Mixed States
authors: Pablo Sala, Vlad Temkin, Cenke Xu, Daniel Podolsky, Ehud Altman
abstract: We develop an operational approach to strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (sw-SSB) of a non-Abelian symmetry group G. We formulate it as the decoding task of distinguishing two strongly symmetric states that differ by a pair of inserted irreps, after both are corrupted by strongly symmetric decoherence. For finite G, this task is dual to distinguishing logical states of the quantum double D(G) under pure-charge noise. We derive a hierarchy of statistical mechanics models describing optimal decoding from the fusion outcomes measured on successively larger nested regions. As for maximum-likelihood decoders of Abelian codes the measured irreps act as quenched disorder obeying a Nishimori-like condition. Strikingly, because local irreps do not determine how they fuse globally, the strong $G\times G$ symmetry is realized only nonlocally, and irreps trivially charged under Z(G) (the center of G) can hide inside noise-generated ones. As a result, the strong symmetry spontaneously breaks down to Z(G), times the weak symmetry. The only transition at nonzero error rate is then an ordering of the center, whose threshold cannot decrease as the hierarchy is ascended. This conclusion holds at any finite level of the hierarchy for non-nilpotent groups. We confirm these predictions with tensor-network calculations for $S_3$ and SU(2). At the first level, the $S_3$ model, whose center is trivial, shows no transition, and the fidelity correlations of all irreps provably decay to non-zero values. The SU(2) model exhibits a $Z_2$ transition consistent with the Nishimori-Ising universality class, where the fidelity correlations of spin-$1/2$ irreps become long-range. The threshold rises from the first to the second level of the hierarchy by $16\%$. Our results provide a systematic framework for studying non-Abelian sw-SSB and for constructing decoders for non Abelian topological codes.
summary: This work introduces an operational method to study spontaneous symmetry breaking in non-Abelian quantum systems by framing it as a decoding problem. The authors derive a hierarchy of statistical models based on measuring fusion outcomes across nested regions. They demonstrate that the symmetry breaking transition is robustly characterized by the center of the group and can be quantified by analyzing the scaling of fidelity correlations.
main_problem: The paper develops an operational framework to study strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (sw-SSB) in non-Abelian quantum systems.
main_result: The symmetry breaking is characterized by an ordering transition in the center of the symmetry group, which is measurable via fidelity correlations. The critical threshold for this transition increases as more local fusion outcomes are incorporated into the decoding process.
method: The analysis uses statistical mechanics models derived from optimal decoding tasks, formulated as partition functions over fusion outcomes measured on nested regions of a fusion tree.
model_or_system: The model involves non-Abelian mixed states corrupted by decoherence, analyzed using symmetries of groups like $S_3$ and $SU(2)$. The decoding task is dual to distinguishing logical states of the quantum double $D(G)$.
key_observables: Uhlmann fidelity, fidelity correlations, and the critical probability threshold ($p_c$) for symmetry restoration.
important_parameters: The hierarchy level ($N$) of fusion measurements, the symmetry group ($G$), and the error rate ($p$).
main_assumptions: The optimal measurement protocol must be non-local for non-Abelian symmetries, and the analysis relies on mapping the decoding problem to statistical mechanics partition functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fusion tree structure for Abelian vs. Non-Abelian groups, and show finite-size scaling of the correlator ratio $D$ for $SU(2)$ at different hierarchy levels, confirming a $Z_2$ transition.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the decoding problem, derives the statistical mechanics models for optimal decoding across a hierarchy of measurements, and then applies these tools to $S_3$ and $SU(2)$ to analyze the symmetry breaking transition.
why_interesting: It provides a systematic, quantitative framework for understanding how local measurements constrain global symmetries in quantum systems, connecting concepts from topological quantum error correction to critical phenomena.
